title: Site rules for a cold-storage warehouse

blocks.text: A cold-storage warehouse (not GridCap) plans each day with a handful of decisions, made for you by `site_variables(model)`: four Booleans (`night`, `freezer`, `dock_a`, `dock_b`) and three counts (`night_staff` from 0 to 20, `frozen_orders` from 0 to 500, `forklifts` from 0 to 6). The site manager's rules:

($`\land`$ is AND.) Write `add_site_rules(model, v, min_night, forklifts_both)` in `site_rules.py`, where `v` is the dict `site_variables` returns. Each rule is one linear row switched by the right literals; no big-M. The tests fix some decisions and ask CP-SAT whether the rules allow them. Four lines.

from __future__ import annotations

from ortools.sat.python import cp_model


def site_variables(model: cp_model.CpModel) -> dict:
    """The warehouse's decisions for one day."""
    return {
        "night": model.new_bool_var("night"),            # the night shift runs
        "freezer": model.new_bool_var("freezer"),        # the freezer room is open
        "dock_a": model.new_bool_var("dock_a"),          # dock A is open
        "dock_b": model.new_bool_var("dock_b"),          # dock B is open
        "night_staff": model.new_int_var(0, 20, "night_staff"),
        "frozen_orders": model.new_int_var(0, 500, "frozen_orders"),
        "forklifts": model.new_int_var(0, 6, "forklifts"),
    }


def add_site_rules(model: cp_model.CpModel, v: dict, min_night: int, forklifts_both: int) -> None:
    """The site rules, each a linear row switched by literals."""
    model.add(v["night_staff"] >= min_night).only_enforce_if(v["night"])
    model.add(v["night_staff"] == 0).only_enforce_if(~v["night"])
    model.add(v["frozen_orders"] == 0).only_enforce_if(~v["freezer"])
    model.add(v["forklifts"] >= forklifts_both).only_enforce_if(v["dock_a"], v["dock_b"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    model = cp_model.CpModel()
    v = site_variables(model)
    add_site_rules(model, v, 4, 3)
    model.maximize(v["frozen_orders"] - 10 * v["forklifts"])
    solver = cp_model.CpSolver()
    print(solver.status_name(solver.solve(model)), {k: solver.value(x) for k, x in v.items()})

import logging

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from ortools.sat.python import cp_model

from site_rules import add_site_rules, site_variables


def check(**fixed):
    model = cp_model.CpModel()
    v = site_variables(model)
    add_site_rules(model, v, 6, 2)
    for name, value in fixed.items():
        model.add(v[name] == value)
    solver = cp_model.CpSolver()
    solver.parameters.max_time_in_seconds = 5
    return solver.status_name(solver.solve(model))


print("min_night 6, night with 7 staff:", check(night=1, night_staff=7))
print("min_night 6, night with 3 staff:", check(night=1, night_staff=3))
print("no night, 2 staff:", check(night=0, night_staff=2))
print("freezer shut, 40 frozen orders:", check(freezer=0, frozen_orders=40))
print("forklifts_both 2, both docks, 1 forklift:", check(dock_a=1, dock_b=1, forklifts=1))
print("forklifts_both 2, dock A only, 1 forklift:", check(dock_a=1, dock_b=0, forklifts=1))

cases.says: a night shift with its minimum crew is allowed, and one short-staffed is refused
a closed freezer with no frozen orders is allowed, and one with orders is refused
two open docks with enough forklifts are allowed, and with too few are refused
either dock open alone needs no extra forklifts
a day with no night shift has no night staff
an open freezer may take frozen orders

origin.section: OnlyEnforceIf Switches a Linear Row On a Conjunction of Literals

concepts: only_enforce_if switches a linear row on when all its literals are true, with no big-M
a literal is a Boolean variable or its negation, written with the tilde operator
